record.paper_title: Open questions in quarkonium and electromagnetic probes
record.context_brief: Nature of the psi-prime suppression anomaly
record.original_question: What is the physical origin of the extra suppression seen in ψ′ production when moving from proton-nucleus collisions to sulphur-uranium and lead-lead collisions: is it caused by ordinary matter effects, melting of charmonium states in a quark-gluon plasma, the onset of the critical energy density already in peripheral heavy-ion collisions at SPS energies, or some other mechanism?

evidence.quote: At this moment, and the situation is not likely to change in the coming years, we cannot say what is the nature of the "anomaly" seen in the ψ′ suppression pattern between the p-A and the S-U/Pb-Pb colliding systems; maybe the extra suppression is due to the matter produced in the heavy-ion collisions; maybe that matter is in the QGP phase and "melts" the c ar c bound states; maybe this indicates that the critical energy density is reached already in the most peripheral S-U or Pb-Pb collisions at the SPS energies; maybe...

artifact.status_search_result: The ψ′ suppression pattern observed at the CERN SPS has been actively studied by NA38/NA50/NA60 and modeled with comover absorption, color screening/QGP melting, and hot hadronic matter scenarios. No single mechanism has been unambiguously identified as the cause of the extra ψ′ suppression seen from p-A to S-U/Pb-Pb collisions; competing interpretations remain viable in the literature, and the question is generally regarded as still open.

status_evidence.title: Experiments revisit the quark-gluon soup – CERN Courier
status_evidence.snippet: Sharp reduction in J/psi and psi prime yields observed in high energy-density collisions, attributed to plasma conditions preventing cc̄ binding.
status_evidence.claim: ψ′ suppression in heavy-ion collisions at SPS is discussed in the context of QGP formation, with the underlying mechanism still under investigation.

status_evidence.title: J/psi production in Indium-Indium collisions (NA60)
status_evidence.snippet: NA60 tested the NA50 interpretation of charmonium suppression in Pb-Pb with In-In data to clarify the role of ordinary versus deconfined matter.
status_evidence.claim: The origin of anomalous charmonium suppression at SPS remained under active investigation, with no definitive identification of the responsible mechanism.

status_evidence.title: Future facilities: the CERN SPS
status_evidence.snippet: Charmonium suppression measurements at SPS continue to be discussed as part of the QGP signature program.
status_evidence.claim: The interpretation of ψ′ suppression at SPS energies has not been definitively resolved.
